Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Work & responsibility

undertake verb

take on a task

also take on, take upon oneself, undertake to do

classical

Cic. Off. 1.28: aut labōrem aut sūmptūs suscipere nōlunt

suscipiō, suscipere, suscēpī, susceptum

verb, third conjugation

undertake, take on

Of a task, a burden, an expense, a war, taken on of one’s own accord; recipere is used of a task one is given or has promised (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • recipiō, recipere, recēpī, receptum — undertake, take on (a duty, a promise); guarantee

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 26: mihi Siculōrum causam receptam, populī Rōmānī susceptam esse videor (Lewis & Short)

    Its first sense is to take back; in sē recipere, to take upon oneself (see undertake responsibility).

  • aggredior, aggredī, aggressus sum — set about, attempt

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Also to approach someone, and to attack.

  • in sē cōnferre (+ infinitive) — take upon oneself (to)

    also used · modern · Traupman 109

    Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence. The classical verbs are suscipere and recipere (above).

Examples

  • Nam aut inimīcitiās aut labōrem aut sūmptūs suscipere nōlunt

    for they are unwilling to take on enmities, or work, or expenseCic. Off. 1.28

See also undertake responsibility, begin, try.
